svg.title: Hold the requests back, then multiply once
svg.desc: On the left eight arriving requests each get their own 23-millisecond forward pass at p99 94 milliseconds and 156 requests per second; on the right the same eight are held in a five-millisecond batch window and run as one 31-millisecond pass at p99 78 and 289 rps, with 5.9 times fewer kernel launches; below, a three-by-three grid of measured throughput and p99 for two serving stacks at batch sizes one, eight and thirty-two with the batch-32 TF Serving cell circled at 2.3x, payload bars for REST JSON, gRPC and base64 JPEG, and a shadow-traffic sketch.
svg.text: Hold the requests back, then multiply once
8 x 23 ms of work, 8 kernel launches
the same eight, held for 5 ms
one 224x224x3 float32 image, on the wire
...or just send the JPEG. 53x smaller than
...and if a request could join a batch already running? -> Week 26, vLLM
